title: finding(ci): `board-snapshot.yml` tells adopters 「there is nothing to configure」 while hard-coding `objectstack/` into a `--delete` R2 sync — two repos on one bucket erase each other's boards
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/board-snapshot.yml` tells a sibling repository to copy it **unchanged** and that **「There is nothing to configure」**. Both sentences are falsified by the same file: the R2 mirror target and the daily tarball key **hard-code `objectstack/`**, while the sync carries `--delete`.

⇒ two repositories adopting this workflow against one bucket share a **single `--delete` sync target**. Each run erases the other board's objects, and the daily tarball goes to whichever ran first. ⚠️ It fires the moment an adopter's maintainer sets the four R2 secrets — which the adoption card explicitly anticipates as a normal, expected maintainer action.

## Measured at source, `origin/main`

```
:129  # There is nothing to configure. The board archived is `github.repository`,
:250          PM_SWEEP_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}          ← the BOARD is parameterised
:359          mirror="s3://${R2_BUCKET}/objectstack/board/"     ← hard-coded
:385            --delete --no-progress \
:407          tarball="s3://${R2_BUCKET}/objectstack/snapshots/${day}.tar.gz"  ← hard-coded
```

⭐ `:250` is the control that makes this a **defect rather than a design**: the file already knows how to parameterise by repository, and does so for the one thing the adopt section mentions. It simply did not do it for the two places that decide **where the bytes land**.

## ⭐ The evidence that it is an oversight, not a choice

The same file reasons carefully about `--delete` blast radius — **within one repository** — at `:370-376`:

> `--delete` is kept and needs no migration step of its own … ⛔ The target is never widened to `objectstack/` to achieve the same mapping — that would put `objectstack/snapshots/` inside a `--delete` target and **eat the daily tarballs**, the failure …

⇒ the author thought hard about exactly this class of accident and bounded it to one board. Two boards on one bucket is the same accident one level up, and nothing in the file considers it.

## How it was found

An adopter hit it. objectui#9387 copied this workflow into `objectstack-ai/objectui`; the executing dev refused to carry the prefix verbatim and changed it to `objectui/`, judging that leaving it would be knowingly shipping silent cross-repository data destruction. The reviewing seat **verified the readings above at source** and adopted that divergence as necessary. ⇒ 「copy unchanged」 is the instruction that was wrong, and the first adopter had to break it to be safe.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ NOT measured: whether any two repositories are pointed at one bucket **today**. The defect is that the documented adoption path leads there, and that the file's own text tells the adopter there is nothing to change.
- ⛔ Not a claim that the `--delete` inside one repository is wrong. It is argued for in the file and the argument holds; only its scope does not.
- ⛔ Not a finding against objectui#9387 or its PR objectui#10203 — that adopter is the reason this is measured rather than latent.

## Suggested shape

Derive the prefix from `github.repository` the way `PM_SWEEP_REPO` already is (`:250`), so a copy is correct with nothing to change — or, if a shared prefix is deliberate, say in the adopt section that it is **the one thing an adopter must change**, and ⛔ delete 「There is nothing to configure」.

Dedupe words: `board-snapshot` · `R2 prefix` · `adopt list` · `sibling repo` · `objectstack/board` · `--delete cross-repo`
